## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-23 BU round: the Self-Repair Trap judge's input reachability domain was never disclosed - 5935 rows all say "not suspected", and two of its three signals received 0 rows of input archive-wide (no LLM, $0)

The judge (`src/tools/self_repair_trap.py:104/:106/:113`) gates each signal on a minimum point count (**3 / 2 / 2**) that never reached the report, so "3200 rows carry a single point and cannot enter any gate", "2723 rows do reach the collapse gate and really read clean" and "the declining and score signals were fed **0** rows archive-wide" all render as the same number. ### What changed

- New `experiments/_trap_input_domain.py`: single source of truth for the judge's input semantics - key-name constants, `SIGNAL_MIN_POINTS` (3/2/2) and `GLOBAL_MIN_POINTS`, the four `BUCKET_*` tiers (not recorded / malformed / below floor / floor reached), retrieval **character-for-character identical** to the judge (`parse_ok` gates a point, `or 0` folds blanks, `bool` never counts as a mutation score), plus `signal_domains` / `input_bucket` / `two_point_decline_outside_domain`.

- `analyze_results`: `per_baseline.self_repair_trap_domain` plus the new "Self-Repair Trap judge input reachability" section (13-column table / silent-arm note / empty-domain note / re-run-error note / two caliber footnotes), with every threshold rendered **from `SIGNAL_MIN_POINTS`** rather than a literal.
- **The judge was not touched**: re-running it in-process against the archived histories gives **0 mismatches** (`reconciled=True`), so this round only adds parallel disclosure - no passed / repair / denominator moves and no new exit for paper numbers.
- Also closed (pre-existing documentation defects): three rows of the status register's **§1 snapshot table** (tests / line coverage / branch coverage) were still stamped **BQ round** - BR, BS and BT never advanced them - now refreshed from measurement without rewriting what those three rounds wrote; §3.2 has no rows for BQ or BT (the BO row recorded the same shape of drift for BN), registered rather than back-filled; and `CHANGELOG.md` / `CHANGELOG.en.md` `Last updated` lines also stopped at BQ - **the head summary chain and the H2 body sequence can diverge indefinitely, because the gate only counts H2 headings**. Two more of the same family surfaced this round: the date line of `docs/INDEX.en.md` also stopped at BQ - `check_bilingual_docs.py --strict` is the only gate that sees it, and only when the paired dates disagree, so a single side lagging is nobody's problem - now rolled to 2026-10-23 with a row for the BU booklet, while the missing EN rows for the BR / BS / BT booklets are registered, not back-filled here; and the `Last updated` head line of `docs/MEASUREMENT_INTEGRITY.md` likewise stopped at BQ although §62–§64 were appended, so §65 is added together with the head roll and those three rounds are recorded as existing drift.

The four keys enter no judgment (no pass / reject / denominator reads them); every number in the section and the summary line is disclosure, not a gate. The existing `per_baseline` key set gains exactly one key (`check_leg_measurability`) and no existing section changes a line (3 of the 65 new locks pin "judgment did not move" specifically).

- 65 new locks = `tests/test_bq_check_leg_readers.py` (identities 25 / seven grades 14 / render disclosure 9 / source anchors 5 / unmeasurable-row semantics 4 / two-grade reason 3 / judgment unchanged 3 / batch summary 2, including parametrized expansions; per-class counts from `--collect-only`); 0 existing assertions rewritten; five suites together 219 passed / 0 failed.

- Gate chain: one full chain each on the dirty tree and the clean tree, 19/19 steps rc=0, 233s total wall clock on both (format 999 files, mypy 137, zero-assert 461 files 0 violations, ast-guards 136/78/20/0/20/19, status-persistence 10 channels 3 persistence surfaces fully covered, json-strict flipped from the pre-existing red to green).

### Boundaries (registered by name)

The four keys appear 0 times in the archive, so this round's reader only emits "unrecorded" for historical artifacts - real grade readings await the next batch; the three raw-side keys (`detection_first_status` / `edit_intent_status` / `deterministic_repair_status`, with `check_status` nested inside `edit_intent_status`) still have no readers; the `or []` fold at `refresh_patch_field.py:201` is unfixed; the root cause of gates being blind to untracked files is unfixed (adding `--others` to the scan surface is a next-round candidate). See the handbook section 7.



> BO closed the raw read side. This round asked what the same `details` rows are read as **when they are
> actually compared**. Two consumers send one kind of absence two different ways, and the renderer quotes
> both: one records nothing, the other folds it into `unknown`, and the difference between the two tables is
> exactly the rows that disappeared.

### Fixed - three sites plus one caliber fix; no judgement value or direction moves

- **1 Absence graded** (`experiments/analysis_parts/cross_analysis.py`): before `if not level: continue` the
  four shapes are counted as `key_absent` / `value_null` / `value_blank` / `other_falsy`, and the result now
  carries `n_details` / `unobserved` / `unobserved_total`; `available=False` splits into `no_rows` (really no
  rows) and `no_level_recorded` (rows exist, no level was ever recorded). Archive: **159** batch files carrying
  the key / **320** arms, `key_absent` **2093** rows, null 0, exact empty string 0, and **122** arms with
  `available=False` - all of them "rows exist but no field at all".
- **2 The delta stops being an absent key** (same file): when a bucket is missing,
  `high_vs_low_success_delta` is now an **explicit `None`** and `delta_missing_buckets` names the missing
  bucket. Of **198** comparable arms in the archive, **0** carry a delta: 157 miss both buckets, 41 miss high.
- **3 The report states both calibers** (`experiments/analyze_results.py`, section 5.3): the "not in the
  comparison" column adds the unrecorded row count, silent arms are named per arm with "N rows, none recorded"
  (instead of the section vanishing), every `N/A` cell says which bucket is missing, and when no arm yields a
  delta the section appends "the >=0.2 / <=0.2 criterion cannot be applied on this data".
- **4 The other consumer becomes subtractable** (`experiments/statistical_analysis.py`): `counts` and both
  rates unchanged (batch-IX caliber kept), new `unknown_of_which_absent` plus a footnote make
  `view.unknown = real unknown rows + cross.unobserved_total` a checkable equation - measured on **320/320**
  arms, as is `sum(by_level.tasks) + unobserved_total == n_details`.
- **5 Caliber fix**: `value_blank` counts only the **exact empty string**. The first draft used
  `not level.strip()`, which counted `" "` as absent - but on the batch-IX side `" "` is truthy and forms its
  own bucket, so the identity breaks by 1 on any corpus containing one, and the archive happens to contain
  **0** such rows: **the probe and the real corpus shared the blind spot**. With the fixed predicate the
  identity holds unconditionally, pinned by its own case.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BN round: the status channels were disclosed at runtime and appeared 0 times in the archived artifacts — the "how to read it" was dropped at both persistence boundaries (zero LLM, $0)

> Five rounds (BH→BM) turned each "unreadable ⇒ favourable" face into a four-valued `status` and wired the
> double read into the judgment side. This round asks the question one step earlier: **do those channels ever
> reach disk?** For three of them they do not. Of the 10 `_status` / `_outcomes` channels declared in
> `src/graph/state.py::AITesterState`, 7 appear in neither the raw-artifact whitelist nor the matching result-row
> branch, and a census of the existing archive (1700 JSON files, 1121 of them raw, plus 9096 JSONL trace rows)
> finds those 7 keys **0 times in 0 files**. In one line: **every disclosure the previous rounds added only ever
> lived in memory — nothing in the archive answers "was this `findings=[]` clean, or did the check crash?"**

### Fixed — filing them back, not changing any verdict

- **① The raw-artifact whitelist carried no check channel** (`experiments/run_benchmark.py::_dump_state_artifacts`):
  the read-only probe measured **5 runtime states (`ok` / `error` / `unavailable` / `disabled` / key absent)
  → 1 archived shape of 558 bytes** — "the check ran and found nothing" was byte-identical to "the check crashed /
  was disabled by design / this concept did not exist in that round". All 10 declared channels are now registered
  in the whitelist (`:936-945`), passed through verbatim via `final_state.get(...)`.
- **② The result row's "5 states → 5 shapes" was an artifact of `contract_status` standing there alone**
  (same file, `_build_task_result`): measured jointly the row boundary looked healthy; **measured per channel** it
  shows the static / safety / oracle pairs folding at the row too (artifact 1 / row 1), and the failure branch's
  3135 characters carried exactly one status channel. The success branch now gains 6 keys and the failure branch
  the same 6 as `None` placeholders (keeping both branches' key sets isomorphic); after the change the failure row
  is 3315 characters carrying 7 channel keys and all four channel groups read 5/5.
  **Lesson: a joint shape count only reflects the keys that are present *and* carrying a difference — a single
  already-registered key is enough to prop the count up.**
- **③ New gate `scripts/gates/check_status_persistence.py` (same ratchet family as BK, but with an empty quota)**:
  the declared surface (the 10 keys in `AITesterState.__annotations__` ending in `_status` / `_outcomes`) must appear
  in **every** persistence surface (raw whitelist + both result-row branches). Current reading: 10 declared channels,
  3 persistence surfaces, fully covered. The difference from BK is deliberate: BK's `EXEMPT` is a *shrinking legacy
  quota*, BN's is *empty* — "declared but never persisted" earns no legacy allowance in this repository.
  A `**helper(...)` spread counts only when it can be resolved statically; unresolvable spreads are simply not
  credited: **a false red beats a false green** (if the row is ever assembled dynamically, the gate turns red,
  not green). Wired in: a `status-persistence` Makefile target added to the `gates` prerequisite segment plus an
  independent blocking step in ci.yml.
- **Default semantics**: in new batches after this round, a channel that was never written lands as `null`; a written
  channel lands with its real value. History is not rewritten, so the archive keeps its 0 occurrences —
  **this round only buys reviewability for future batches**.

### Tests — 54 new cases (`tests/test_bn_status_persistence.py`)

Declared surface 3 / raw whitelist 21 / result row 19 / four-valued vocabulary 2 / ratchet self-test 6 / wiring 3.

**`make gates` ran green end to end twice** (first run before this backfill, wall clock **200s**; the run after

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BM round: the experiment and report read sides folded "the check never ran / the check crashed" into the most favourable value of their domain — a crash filed into the "clean" group, an unmeasured row filed into "zero regressions" (zero LLM, $0)

> BL closed the double-read caliber inside `src/` and its registered boundary said out loud that
> `experiments/` was not done — this round is that piece. In one line: **on the two read-side tables
> of the experiments and the reports, "this leg never measured" was still written as "it measured,
> and nothing was wrong"**, and the spelling was even more direct than in `src/` — the crash branch
> returned the **most favourable** value of its domain.

### Fixed — four read-side folds: no seat in the favourable group, no flip of the judgment direction

- **① The contamination crash leg returned `low`** (`experiments/run_benchmark.py`,
  `_compute_contamination_risk_level`): the `except Exception` tail `return "low"` became
  `return "unknown"`. Downstream, `low` **is** the clean group
  (`statistical_analysis.contamination_view_summary` files `low` under `clean_n` /
  `clean_passed_rate`, and `analysis_parts/cross_analysis.high_vs_low_success_delta` uses the `low`
  bucket as the comparison baseline), so "this leg crashed" was registered as "checked, no overlap
  evidence". **This is a missed half-fix, not a new design**: the inner `_combined_risk_level`
  (`contamination_check.py:299`) already gained an `unknown` grade back in O22 (2026-09-29 review P1)
  for exactly this, its docstring reading verbatim "previously a missing patch / missing gold /
  **exceptions all fail open into "low"**, which produced the zero-discriminating 100% `low` over
  852 rows (580 of them an empty-string patch)" — the inner function was fixed, the wrapper never
  followed; and both consumers had long since excluded `unknown` honestly from both denominators
  (`ADR-0023` states that not_applicable/unknown do not enter the denominator).
- **② `contract_status` was written on the experiment side and read by nobody** (same file,
  `_build_risk_summary_for_result`): BL wrote the status into the experiment-side result row, yet
  the argument list of `build_risk_summary(...)` did not contain it ⇒ BL's new
  `contract_unmeasurable(...)` disclosure **never appears** in the `risk_summary` the experiments
  emit, and `risk_summary["contract_status"]` stayed `None` (since BL both branches literally write
  the key; the argument is what decides its value). The success branch now passes
  `contract_status=final_state.get("contract_status")` (`run_benchmark.py:2394`), the failure branch
  keeps `None`. **`risk_score`, level and factors are byte-identical** — one more disclosure, nothing else.
- **③ The all-row denominator behind R4/N1** (`experiments/run_main_batch.py._print_r4_summary`):
  the numerator counted only rows `== 1.0` while the denominator was `n = len(det)`, which includes
  rows whose `regression_rate` is `None` and rows that do not carry the key at all ⇒ unmeasured rows
  scored as "no regression / no test error", and `0.0%` happened to read as "zero regressions". The
  denominator is now the measurable row count (`regr_k` / `te_k`) and the line prints "measurable
  k/n"; when `k=0` it prints `不可测（无可测行）（可测 0/3）` instead of `0.0%`. **The three M1 metrics in
  the same print block already used `m1_denom`** — two calibers inside one block is the morphological
  source of this defect. The numerator is untouched.
- **④ Section 5.3 swallowed three grades whole** (`experiments/analyze_results.py`): rendering
  high-vs-low took only `by_risk_level["high"]` and `["low"]`, so `medium` / `unknown` /
  `not_applicable` neither entered the comparison nor left any count ⇒ the reader cannot know how
  many rows the comparison stands on. The table gains a "未入对照任务" column (the three grades
  totalled) plus one caliber note.

### Measurement

- **Crash-leg reachability grid, 15 inputs** (the try body re-executed in-process to capture the real
  exception, Python 3.14.6): before the change the distribution was
  `{'high': 1, 'medium': 2, 'low': 12, 'unknown': 0}`, **5/15** legs crashed and **all five folded
  into `low`** (bytes / list / dict / int / non-string gold side; plus a hand-built `sys.modules`
  poisoning leg, 6/16 overall). The same grid after the change reads
  `{'high': 1, 'medium': 2, 'low': 7, 'unknown': 5}` and "favourable (`low`) and from a crash leg = **[]**".
  **The string side is unreachable by a constructive argument**, not just "ran it, saw no red":
  `_TOKEN_RE` (`contamination_check.py:56`) keeps only identifiers and numbers and drops every
  punctuation character, so the pseudo-code assembled from the skeleton can at most make `ast.parse`
  raise `SyntaxError` (already caught by the inner `(SyntaxError, ValueError)`), the `tokenize`
  fallback carries its own `(TokenError, IndentationError, SyntaxError)` guard, `_embed_code` swallows
  everything, and `_lcs_ratio` / `_token_bag_cosine` only eat already-normalised token lists.
- **Two archive denominators registered separately (never cross-quoted)**: the row-level census
  (recursively expanding **1700** files under `experiments/results/**/*.json`) finds
  `contamination_risk_level` at **8865** sites = 7843 `not_applicable` + 1022 `low`, with
  `unknown` / `high` / `medium` at **0** each; among the patch field shapes **non-string patches are 0
  rows** ⇒ the crash leg has **0 real instances** in the archive and the value change in ① touches no
  published number. The batch-summary caliber (only the `results.<bl>.details` lists) is 259 files
  whose raw bytes contain `"details"` / **335** (batch, baseline) combinations / **11197** rows. All
  108 `JSONDecodeError` files are
  `_superseded_20261010/.../quixbugs_filtered/json_testcases/*.json` (test-case data, not result
  rows) and a raw-byte scan shows **0 of them carry the key** ⇒ the denominator is complete.
- **The R4/N1 denominator gap (11197 rows)**: `regression_rate` — 3185 key-absent + 8012 `None` ⇒ **0**
  measurable rows, while the old caliber printed `0.0%` "zero regressions" forever; `test_error_rate`
  — 3185 key-absent + 806 `None` ⇒ **7206** measurable rows (814 of them `1.0`), old caliber **7.3%** →
  measurable caliber **11.3%**. Per baseline: `aitester` 6.6%→10.9% (k=3513/5819), `plain_llm`
  6.5%→10.4% (1304/2081), `plain_llm_df` 10.7%→11.6% (2129/2300), `single_agent` **6.7%→94.0%**
  (50/697 — 47 of its 50 measurable rows are `=1.0`). The `94.0%` is **a new number produced by
  switching the denominator**, not "regressions got worse"; differencing it against the historical
  `6.7%` is a caliber error.
- **Why `regression_rate` reads a constant 0.0% — a diagonal, not a measurement**: all 11197 rows carry
  `task_metadata`; crossing P2P material against key presence, the **184** rows with a non-empty
  `pass_to_pass` **all omit the key**, and the 8012 rows that write `None` all lack the material
  ⇒ the intersection is empty ⇒ the archive contains no row that is both measurable and valued (the
  only measurable precondition is the `p2p_tests` guard at `_m1_metrics.py:990`).

### Boundaries (named, not written off)

- `analysis_parts/cross_analysis.py:42` does `if not level: continue`, so a row **missing the field**
  does not even count as `observed`, while `statistical_analysis` folds a missing field into `unknown`.
  The two calibers disagree and this is **known and unresolved**: unifying them would change the
  meaning of `available=False` (batches with no such field at all would start rendering an empty
  table), which is a judgment-direction change, so this round only states the difference in the docstring.
- **The crash leg still has 0 real production instances** (0 non-string patches in the archive). This
  round registers "5 hand-built grid inputs + 1 import-poisoning leg + 0 archive instances", the same
  honest caliber as BK: the locks defend "a future crash gets no favourable grade", not "it crashed before".
- The `unknown` trigger of `_combined_risk_level` (empty `values`) was not touched; on the wrapper path
  that grade can only arise from a crash leg or an empty value.
- `experiments/` and `scripts/` remain outside mutation / ratchet coverage (registered in BK); these
  four sites are guarded by the 32 locks.
- `risk_summary["contract_status"]` appears **0** times across the 8865 archived rows (BL was the
  round that wrote the key into `build_risk_summary`) ⇒ ② changes no historical JSON, only batches
  run from now on.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BL round: the publish side already carried a status, the judgment side still read the empty value — "never measured" was read as "measured and clean" (zero LLM, $0)

> Rounds BH→BK wrote "unreadable" into observability keys, but nobody ever checked whether the
> judgment side reads them. Measured this round: before the fix, the key-name judgment reads of the
> `contract_status` channel were **0**, and `assess_task_risk` did not even have a `contract_status`
> parameter. Fields are cheap; readers are the close-out.

### Fixed — per-leg status, double reads on the consumer side, and a 12th failure pattern

- **New primitive `status_for_check(outcomes, check)`** (`src/utils/check_status.py:161`): worst-of over
  one leg only, and **no record ⇒ `None`**. `safety_check_status` aggregates two independent pre-checks
  (naming contract + dangerous API), so letting the aggregate speak for the contract leg files
  "dangerous-API leg unreadable" under the contract's name (mutation anchor M17 locks this in reverse).
- **Five consumer sites**: `risk_approval._contract_disclosure:123` (text only when status is non-empty
  and ≠ ok) + `_impact_factor:142/173` (**appends to the note; `factor` byte-for-byte unchanged**) +
  `assess_task_risk:202/242` (pass-through plus `logger.warning("G2 … not evidence (verdict unchanged)")`) +
  `build_risk_summary:284` (**both** the enabled and disabled branches write `contract_status`,
  `:326` `:352`) + `graph/debugger.py:918` (the call site takes the channel value; without it the four
  parameters above are decoration).
- **Two more readers**: `agents/debugger.py:795` turns `static_check_status not in (None, CHECK_OK)` into a
  warning (until now that caliber existed only as a comment nobody executed); `patch_applier.py:507`
  takes the S2 leg's own status and discloses it while leaving the `added` return value untouched.
- **Observability**: `agent_telemetry` gains `_UNMEASURABLE_STATUS_KEYS` (5 channels) ×
  `_UNMEASURABLE_STATUSES` (`error` / `unavailable`) and `_pattern_check_unmeasurable`, registered as the
  **12th** failure pattern `check_unmeasurable` → MAST `Inadequate verification`; `_flatten_record` now
  lifts the inner `output` keys of trace records, otherwise the pattern could never see
  `oracle_check_status`.
- **Four publish sites completed**: `nodes.py:2867` per-leg channel, `nodes.py:1478` trace payload now
  carries `oracle_check_status`, `run_benchmark.py:1869` success rows carry `contract_status`,
  `state.py:371` declares the channel.
- **`None` is not `error`**: the first means "this leg did not run", the second "this leg could not be
  measured". Counting `None` as unmeasurable would re-judge all 8853 `None` archive rows — the archive
  probe is written as "keys entirely absent ⇒ no hit".

### Verification

- **Verdict values and verdict direction unchanged, byte for byte**: no new "reject because status is
  bad" branch; every disclosure assertion in the locks is paired with "the text changed, the verdict did
  not", and the mutation side locks it in reverse (M6 turns disclosure into a verdict change, M16 turns
  S2 into a refusal) — both must be red.
- **Census (after, deduped caliber with per-key reconciliation = True)**: `contract_status`
  publish=6 / judgment reads=4 / declaration=1, `contract_missing_symbols` judgment reads=3; variable
  caliber (A2) `static_check_status` 0 → **2**, `oracle_check_status` 0 → **1**; parameter caliber (D)
  **22** reader functions / **76** reads / **5** explicit comparisons, `status_for_check` call sites **2**;
  vocabulary caliber (D2) **58** `CHECK_*` sites (12 operator / 46 call-arg). The before-reading used the
  pre-dedup instrument, so those deltas contain an instrument change and are not registered as code
  movement — only the three name-level comparable tables are (see §3.1 and the booklet).
- **Zero impact on history**: `experiments/results/**/*.json` — **1702 files / 1594 parsed / 108
  `JSONDecodeError`**, all five status channel keys appear **0** times; `contract_missing_symbols`
  appears 8865 times = 8853 `None` + 12 non-empty (len 1×9 / 3×1 / 5×2), value distribution identical
  before and after.
- **32 regression locks** (`tests/test_bl_status_readers_outcome.py`, 6 groups: per-leg primitive 5 /
  double read 8 / publish side 6 / dangerous-API consumer 5 / failure pattern 5 / static layer consumer 3).
  Two of them exist because of survivors: iterating the key set from the set under test (M11 survived) and
  the **unreachable** combination "contract ok + dangerous-API error" (M17 survived).
- **Mutation: all 22 anchors killed** (red counts 2/3/1/2/1/3/1/1/1/1/1/3/2/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/1/1) + **neutral control M23 (wording only) 0 red**;
  per-anchor collected counts equal before/after, sha256 byte-exact restore, `# mutation:` residue 0
  (wall 86s).
- Pre-registration run **11703 passed / 1 failed / 5 skipped** (198.00s, with `--cov`; collected 11709):
  the single failure was the baseline-number guard (still 11672); after the refresh the confirming run is
  **11704 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed at 209.29s / rc=0 (39 warnings; collected 11709)**.
- **A caliber incident, not a product regression**: the confirming run passed `--cov` but **not `--cov-branch`**, so it
  overwrote the repo-root `coverage.xml` with a `branches-valid=0` version. In the full-caliber `make test-cov` run that
  followed, the two reconciliation cases in `tests/test_artifact_doc_consistency_gate.py` - which **read that artifact** -
  started against the branch-less file and reported **11702 passed / 2 failed, 210.65s / rc=2**. Handled by re-running that
  file standalone (**32 passed**) and the gate script itself (**rc=0** on the spot), then recomputing the coverage readings
  from a regenerated full-caliber artifact (19393/19904 lines, 7105/7532 arcs). The lesson enters
  `docs/MEASUREMENT_INTEGRITY.md` §56: **a shared artifact's reading belongs to whichever run overwrote it last**, so a
  manual quick run must either point `COVERAGE_FILE` elsewhere or be followed immediately by a same-caliber regeneration;
  two failures get their artifact producer checked before anyone calls them a regression.
- Coverage **19393/19904 lines = 97.4327%**, **7105/7532 arcs = 94.3309%** (97.43 / 94.33 at two
  decimals): denominator +30 lines / covered +30 ⇒ 511 uncovered, digit-for-digit identical to BK;
  denominator +12 arcs / covered +12 ⇒ 427 missing arcs identical. `src/utils/check_status.py`
  **70/70 lines + 24/24 arcs = 100%**, `graph/nodes.py` 852/853 (branch 323/326 = 99.08%; +13 lines / +4 arcs span the
  whole uncommitted BD→BL stack, **not attributed to BL alone**). BK's four-decimal figures corrected in
  passing: 19363/19874 and 7093/7520 divide to **97.4288% / 94.3218%**, not the 97.4300% / 94.3200%
  registered (two-decimal readings unchanged).
- **`make gates` ran green end to end, rc=0, twice** (first run before this backfill, second run after it, each executed alone and never overlapping another pytest run or a doc edit): wall clock **213s / 214s**, **all 18 commands in the chain green**; the chain's pytest (xdist `-n 4 --dist loadfile`, **no `--cov`**) returned the same verdict both times - **11704 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed** (207.16s / 208.34s, 54 / 46 warnings; collected **11709**) - and the per-step gate readings at the tail of the chain are byte-identical between the two runs, the only difference being the hypothesis warning count; after the backfill, every test that reads the docs or `BASELINE.yaml` (38 files, selected by grepping for `BASELINE.yaml|CHANGELOG|README|docs/INDEX|PROJECT_STATUS_REGISTER|MEASUREMENT_INTEGRITY`) re-ran **1037 passed in 52.43s** (both chain runs saw the same tree, so the collection face was collected **11709** in each; after the final run the newest mtime under `src/`, `tests/` and `scripts/` was 08:25:19, earlier than that run's 08:38:36 start, so what still differs from it is only prose and comments) — the same verdict counts as the confirming run above, a different elapsed-time caliber. Chain head: `ruff check` clean, `ruff format --check .` → **974 files already formatted** (digit-for-digit with the out-of-chain re-measure), `mypy src/ config.py` → 0 errors over **137 source files**; `ast-guards` inside the chain reported **136/78/20/0/20/19**, digit-for-digit with BK's out-of-chain self-test (BL touched no `ast.parse` guard surface); `check_artifact_doc_consistency.py`'s register-coverage branch reported `[OK]` (`coverage.xml` is the full-caliber `make test-cov` artifact; the earlier branch-less one is registered above as a caliber incident). Booklet
  `docs/reviews/CONSUMER_SIDE_STATUS_READERS_BL_2026-10-22.md`; lessons in `docs/MEASUREMENT_INTEGRITY.md` §56.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BK round: a capture-surface ratchet for the `ast.parse` guards — "unreadable" has two exception faces, so the caliber gets a gate instead of another memory (zero LLM, $0)

> Rounds BG→BJ each converged one module's static judgment surface, but nobody was watching
> "the next single-leg guard": of the 78 `try` sites in `src/` that call `ast.parse`, 35 caught only
> `SyntaxError`, and this round measured that lone-surrogate text raises `UnicodeEncodeError` (a
> `ValueError` subclass) — which escaped to the caller, while the branches that did degrade folded
> "unreadable" into `[]` / `set()` / the original code / `ok=True`.

### Fixed — capture surface, shape attribution, and a quota for the survivors

- **One new leg, and it is not a syntax problem**: genuine syntax errors, null bytes, fully fenced
  blocks and git diffs all raise `SyntaxError` on 3.14.6; **lone surrogates** raise
  `UnicodeEncodeError`. The capture surface therefore converges by **family** —
  `AST_UNREADABLE_ERRORS = (SyntaxError, ValueError)` in BI's single source of truth
  `src/utils/check_status.py`, which this round grew from 43 to 65 lines / 22 arcs. Enumerating
  exception names is next round's defect.
- **13 sites across 5 modules**: `deterministic_repair` 3 (`_top_level_names` / `_insert_import` /
  `attempt_deterministic_repair`), `cross_file` 2 (`analyze_cross_file_deps` / `_collect_reverse_deps`),
  `patch_intent` 2 (`apply_edit_intents`), `multi_candidate` 5 (`static_validate_patch` /
  `_func_signatures` / `synthesize_candidates` ×3), `expert_pool` 1 (`_normalize_patch_for_voting`).
- **Escape ⇒ conservative rejection plus disclosure** (`static_validate_patch`): the fold direction matches the
  `SyntaxError` branch and **no new pass-through is granted** — a crash is not a judgment; replacing it with
  "rejected, and why" is the disposition.
- **Four shapes**: `fenced_block` / `git_diff` / `undecodable` / `syntax`. Folding `undecodable` into `syntax`
  (mutation anchor M2 is the reverse lock) claims that an encoding problem is a code defect.
- **Three publishers**: `graph/debugger.py:389-390` (deterministic branch), `graph/debugger.py:721-722`
  (expert-pool branch), `agents/debugger.py:690-693` (edit intents), each writing `check_status` (worst-of,
  **empty reading ⇒ `error`**) and `check_outcomes` (a copy of the legs).
- **The gate**: `scripts/gates/check_ast_parse_guards.py` counts per `try` site and asks whether the handler can
  catch the **whole** `ValueError` family, resolving the shared constant's runtime value; wired as the
  `ast-guards` target of `make gates` and a standalone ci.yml step (gate counts 27/25/28 → **28/26/29**).
  `EXEMPT` is a **may-only-shrink** quota (19 entries / 20 sites, each `(site count, fold shape)`): a new
  single-leg guard, an over-quota site, a stale entry and an over-large entry all turn red.

### Verification

- **One ruler, two trees**: current tree 136 files / 78 sites / 20 uncovered / **0 violations** / 20 exempt hits /
  19 entries; the HEAD export 135 files / 79 sites / **35 single-leg / 15 violations** (named one by one, exactly
  13 BK + 2 BJ). The 79 → 78 one-site gap is reconciled by a `(file, function)` multiset and belongs to **earlier
  rounds**: `oracle_validator::check_assertions` 2 → 0 (BJ switched to `parses_as_module()`) and
  `testless_validation::_unparseable_side` 0 → 1 (added by BH/BI).
- **Judgment-invariance harness** (`scripts/tools/bk_judgment_invariance.py`): inputs = 11 grid shapes + 14596
  archive code strings, 11 decision surfaces ⇒ **160677 comparisons**, `identical=160636 / escape_fixed=41 /
  both_raised=0 / UNEXPECTED=0` at `rc=0` (64s wall clock). The 41 escape legs = 9 functions × 4 surrogate shapes
  + 3 `static_validate_patch` + 2 `apply_edit_intents`, **0 from the archive corpus**. Baseline attribution was
  checked per file: the HEAD versions of the five compared modules mention `check_status|outcome_sink` 0 times, and
  the one intruder (BG's `static_check_*` key backfill) sits in `build_deterministic_debug_result`, which is not
  among the compared functions.
- **55 locks** (`tests/test_bk_ast_guard_capture.py`, 10 groups: capture surface 4 / shape attribution 7 /
  deterministic_repair 6 / cross_file 5 / expert_pool 5 / patch_intent 5 / multi_candidate 9 / shared BJ-BK
  vocabulary 2 / publishers 5 / the ratchet itself 7); neighbouring surface 23 files, **collected 644 / 644 passed**.
- **All 13 mutation anchors killed** (red counts 24/15/1/2/1/5/2/2/1/1/1/5/1) + **neutral control 0 red**, zero
  `# bk-mutation` residue, per-anchor sha256 byte restore (54s; collected ranges 55–104 per anchor — this round's
  caliber is "equal before and after the same anchor", not "equal across anchors"). The two widest nets: M1 (24 red)
  also takes down the pre-existing `tests/test_multi_candidate.py`; M12 (5 red) proves the gate's **own self-check**
  is inside the locks.
- Pre-registration run **11670 passed / 2 failed / 5 skipped** (196.40s, with `--cov`; collected **11677**): the two

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BJ round: closing the "unreadable ⇒ no findings" path in the AST assertion-consistency checker — both legs carry a status and the roll-up takes the worst one (zero LLM, $0)

> BI gave the write-time guards a status, but one folding was still open on the
> generator side: `src/tools/oracle_validator.check_assertions` returned
> `findings=[]` for four different facts — "scanned and nothing found", "input
> was empty", "the test text could not be parsed, so nothing was ever scanned",
> "the code under test could not be parsed, so the type-inference channel went
> mute". The consumer `_run_generator_postchecks` read all four as "no findings",
> so O4 — tautological assertion ⇒ mark `test_defect` ⇒ route the task back to
> the Generator, the only write-side path on that side — **never fired for an
> unreadable artefact**.

### Fixed — per-leg status, worst-of roll-up, state channel publication

- **Judgment is untouched by design**: `check_assertions` gained an *optional*
  `outcome_sink` appending `{check, status, reason}` per leg; with `sink=None`
  the return contract is byte-identical, and the invariance claim has an
  observation surface — the old-vs-new `repr(findings)` diff over all **10855**
  corpus artefacts shows **0 differences** (`crashes_old=0 / crashes_new=0`);
- **Two legs**: `assertion_consistency` (`ok:assertions_checked` /
  `ok:no_assert_statements` / `disabled:empty_input` /
  `error:unparseable_test:fenced_block` / `error:unparseable_test:syntax`) and
  `target_type_inference` (`ok:target_parsed` / `disabled:target_not_provided` /
  `error:unparseable_target`), reusing the four-valued vocabulary BI hoisted to
  `src/utils/check_status.py` (this round is its 4th consumer);
- **Three implementation rules, each with a directional lock**: a blind early
  exit **does not record the second leg** (recording it would state a fact about
  a comparison that never ran); the fence attribution test is "**starts with
  three backticks after stripping leading whitespace**", not "three backticks
  appear in the body" — the two spellings differ by exactly **1** site over the
  real corpus, cross-checked by `scripts/tools/bj_discriminator_crosscheck.py`
  (`sites=10855 / unparsable=76 / strict=72 / loose=73 / loose_only=1`), which
  deliberately does not import `src/` so it cannot be polluted by the mutation
  harness; parsing is funnelled through `parses_as_module` — **the only
  behavioural change this round** (a lone surrogate makes `ast.parse` raise
  `UnicodeEncodeError`, a `ValueError` subclass rather than a `SyntaxError`,
  which used to escape through the observation layer);
- **Consumer**: the two legs are independent checks ⇒ a **worst-of** roll-up
  (same direction as BI, opposite to BG's interchangeable backends — both
  directions are locked), a warning naming `check=status:reason` whenever the
  aggregate is not `ok`, and publication of `oracle_check_status` /
  `oracle_check_outcomes`, declared in `src/graph/state.py`'s TypedDict and
  defaulted to `None` because LangGraph silently drops undeclared keys; the key
  names were chosen after a grep found `experiments/oracle_quality_replay.py:1254`
  already using `oracle_status` for the *contract* oracle, with a lock asserting
  the two fields are not the same thing; `oracle_findings` is still written only
  when non-empty (historic behaviour byte-identical).

### Verification

  4 / test-side leg 12 / target-side leg 8 / judgment invariance 17 /
  consumer aggregation 12 / channel publication 7 / state channel 3, including

  itself the evidence that judgment did not move;

  input / let the sink leak into the return value — 7 / 20 / 1 red), M24 is a

- real corpus (re-measured this round): **1702** archive `.json` files (**1594**

  `oracle_findings` / `tautological_count` / `o4_triggered` appear **0** times

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-22 BI round: closing the "unreadable ⇒ passed" path in the two write-time static prechecks — both guards carry a status and the roll-up takes the worst one (zero LLM, $0)

> BD–BH closed the pytest summaries and the checkers' empty findings, but the two
> guards that run between "patch applied" and "written to disk" —
> `src/tools/patch_applier.check_naming_contract` (P0 1.3 symbol guard) and
> `dangerous_api_added` (S2 AST differ) — still returned one value for two very
> different facts: "compared, nothing missing / nothing new" and "the input could
> not be parsed, so no comparison ever happened". `(True, [])` was four things at
> once (clean comparison / unreadable original / unreadable patch with a
> symbol-free original / `PATCH_CONTRACT_CHECK=false`), and the consumer
> `src/graph/nodes.py::_check_patch_safety` read all four as "guard passed".

### Fixed — per-guard status, worst-of roll-up, state channel publication

- **Judgment is untouched by design**: both guards gained an *optional*
  `outcome_sink` that appends `{check, status, reason}`; with `sink=None` the
  return contract is byte-identical, and the corpus-wide old-vs-new diff in
  `tests/test_bi_static_precheck_unmeasurable.py` re-implements the HEAD formula
  to prove it;
- **Vocabulary hoisted** to `src/utils/check_status.py` (single source of truth
  for BD–BH–BI: `ok / disabled / unavailable / error`,
  `CHECK_STATUS_PRECEDENCE`, `parses_as_module`, `unparseable_side`,
  `record_check_outcome`, `worst_check_status`, `any_measurable_status`), with
  locks asserting that the three layers' literals are *character-identical* and
  that the two aggregation directions legitimately differ;
- **Naming contract**: unreadable original ⇒ `error:unparseable_original`
  (still allows, now stating "no symbol comparison was performed"); unreadable
  patch ⇒ `error:unparseable_patched` and the warning text stops claiming "the
  patch deleted N module-level symbols"; switch off / empty input ⇒ `disabled`;
  parseable original with zero module-level symbols ⇒ `ok:no_module_level_symbols`
  (here "nothing to delete" really is evidence);
- **Dangerous-API differ**: unparseable patch ⇒ `error` on the **fail-open** side
  (empty difference means "nothing could be read", not "nothing was added");
  unparseable original ⇒ `error` on the **over-reject** side (every patch hit
  counts as new); empty input ⇒ `disabled`;
- **Consumer**: `_check_patch_safety` aggregates worst-of (the two guards are
  independent checks, so the direction is opposite to BG's interchangeable
  backends), warns `写盘前静态预检可测量性降级（整体 status=…）` naming
  `check=status:reason`, and `_patch_applier_node` publishes
  `safety_check_status` / `safety_check_outcomes`, declared in
  `src/graph/state.py`'s TypedDict and defaulted to `None` because LangGraph
  silently drops undeclared keys;
- **`type_repair_layer`**: its contract loop-back now pairs the historic
  `contract_ok` with `contract_status` / `contract_reason` /
  `contract_outcomes` (`contract_not_evaluated`,
  `contract_enforcement_disabled`, `contract_check_exception`), warning whenever
  the loop-back ran without being able to read the code.

### Verification

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 BH round: closing the "unmeasurable ⇒ verified" path in the four G5 testless validation layers — each layer carries a status and the roll-up takes the worst one (zero LLM, $0)

> After BA–BG closed the pytest-side summaries and the external checkers' empty
> results, the four layers of `src/tools/testless_validation.py` (AST symbol
> guard / mypy / naming contract / import smoke) still folded "this layer never
> measured" and "this layer finished with zero findings" into the same
> `passed=True`: the roll-up recorded `failed_layers` only when `not passed`,
> and both the docstring and the `src/graph/nodes.py` consumer read the value as
> "validation passed". The root cause came from running it — the mypy layer had
> been passing `--silent-imports`, a flag mypy 1.15.0 no longer accepts (live
> run: `rc=2` plus `unrecognized arguments`), so a clean patch, a type error and
> a syntax error all returned the byte-identical "mypy 发现 1 处问题" and the
> layer had never completed one real type check.

### Fixed — per-layer status, worst-layer aggregation, consumer disclosure

- **Root cause**: `--silent-imports` → `--follow-imports=silent`, plus two argv
  assertions (the legacy spelling must not reappear; interpreter and temp file
  are correct) and three end-to-end real-mypy cases whose results differ from
  each other;
- **Each layer** now returns `{passed, status, reason, detail}` with `status` in
  `ok / disabled / unavailable / error` (BG's vocabulary);
- **Roll-up** gains `validation_status` (**worst layer wins**: error >
  unavailable > disabled > ok, unknown or missing treated as error) and
  `degraded_layers`, and warns naming `layer=status:reason` whenever the status
  is not ok. The aggregation direction is the opposite of BG's "any ok ⇒ ok":
  these four layers are independent checks, not interchangeable backends of one
  check;
- **Only undisclosed fake-clean became fail-closed**: mypy `rc ∉ {0,1}`, `rc=1`
  with no parseable finding line, and unparseable input for the AST guard or the
  naming contract all become `error` + `passed=False`; already-disclosed
  degradations (layer switch off, mypy not installed, timeout, `OSError`) keep
  their `passed` value untouched, and the import-smoke dangerous-API refusal is
  recorded as `disabled` (a refusal is a policy, not a measurement);
- **Consumer**: `nodes.py` now states explicitly, when `passed=True` but
  `validation_status != "ok"`, that the result "is not evidence that validation
  passed" (and still does not block the main flow).

### Verification

- `tests/test_bh_testless_validation_status.py` **52 cases** (mypy rc
  classification 10 / argv root-cause locks 2 / real-mypy end-to-end 3 /
  disclosed mypy degradations 5 / AST guard 5 / naming contract 5 / import smoke
  6 / aggregator 8 / roll-up 6 / consumer 2, parameterisation expanded); the
  existing `tests/test_testless_validation.py::TestAstSymbolGuard::test_syntax_error_degrades`
  was rewritten to the new caliber (its old `passed is True` assertion locked
  exactly the fake-clean this round closes; case count unchanged, 21);
- **mutation 11 anchors all red (7/4/1/5/2/1/8/2/1/1/1) + neutral control 0 red**
  (`scripts/tools/bh_mutation_verify.py`, collected 73 throughout, bytes restored
  by sha256);
- Real corpus (re-measured this round): `TESTLESS_VALIDATION_ENABLE` appears at
  **107** sites in **100** archived JSON files, all `null` (plus 17 `.log` files,
  likewise all `null`); the `testless_validation` payload key is present in only
  **2** archives, both `null`; `failed_layers` / `infra_degraded` /
  `validation_status` / `degraded_layers` appear **0** times across **1702**
  archived JSON ⇒ the layer is off by default, historical readings unaffected,
  zero backfill;
- Boundaries: `patch_applier.check_naming_contract`'s three-way `(True, [])`
  return is unchanged (the distinction happens in front of it on the testless
  side); `validation_status` is disclosure, not a blocking policy; the
  `testless_validation` key was already declared in `src/graph/state.py`, so this
  round needed no TypedDict / `debug()` key-set / prompt-card follow-up;
- pre-registration run **11503 passed / 1 failed / 5 skipped, 218.93s**

  pytest 11504 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed, 213.22s; the post-backfill

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 BG round: closing the "unmeasurable ⇒ fake clean" path in static type checking — mypy/pyright outcomes are four-valued, so an empty finding list is not free evidence (zero LLM, $0)

> After BA–BF closed the pytest-side rc==0 verdicts, the external static
> checkers in `src/tools/type_repair.py` still had a sibling channel:
> switch-off / not-installed / timeout / crash / an unexpected exit code /
> a corrupt report all did `return []`, byte-for-byte identical to "the
> check completed and found nothing"; `mypy_findings_count=0` folded four
> states into one 0, so "the checker did not run" read as "the patch is
> type-clean". pyright was looser: with `--outputjson` lacking
> `generalDiagnostics`, the old `report.get(...) or []` silently treated
> the report as empty. Each attempt now records `{backend, status, reason}`
> through `outcome_sink`, with status `ok / disabled / unavailable / error`;
> the static layer aggregates them into `static_check_status` /
> `static_check_outcomes`.

### Fixed — checker outcomes and observation keys

- **mypy**: switch-off / empty input ⇒ `disabled`; not installed ⇒
  `unavailable`; rc 0/1 ⇒ `ok` (0 = no errors, 1 = errors found; both are
  trustworthy reports); rc≥2 ⇒ `error` `mypy_rc_<n>`; exception ⇒ `error`
  `mypy_exception`.
- **pyright**: switch-off / backend not selected / empty input ⇒
  `disabled`; neither CLI nor package present ⇒ `unavailable`; timeout ⇒
  `error` `pyright_timeout` (outranks every other verdict); rc outside 0/1
  (including `None`) ⇒ `error`; empty stdout / invalid JSON / non-object /
  missing `generalDiagnostics` ⇒ `error`; a trustworthy report ⇒ `ok`.
  Parsed diagnostics are still kept; the text fallback never upgrades empty
  output to `ok`.
- **Aggregation**: any `ok` ⇒ `ok`; otherwise `error` > `unavailable` >
  `disabled`; on `error` a warning names `backend=status:reason`.
- **Observation keys**: `static_check_status` / `static_check_outcomes` are
  declared on the `State` TypedDict and in the initial state, and flow
  through the debugger result; the deterministic repair result mirrors the
  same keys (the key-set contract does not drift).

### Verification

- `tests/test_bg_static_check_outcome.py` **25 cases** (mypy 7 / pyright 12 /
  layer aggregation 4 / state keys 2); the debug key-set contract in
  `tests/test_batch_iv.py` gains the two keys (case count unchanged);
- **mutation 8 anchors all red (1/3/1/2/1/1/3/2) + neutral control 0 red**
  (`scripts/tools/bg_mutation_verify.py`, sha256 byte restore, collected
  constant at 25);
- real corpus: `TYPE_CHECK_ENABLE` is off by default and **170/170** archived
  results record it as `null`, with the experiment env snapshot the only
  listing ⇒ zero impact on historical readings, zero backfill;

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AZ round: a statistic's scale and tail must not be rewritten by the implementation — Cohen's g back to 0–0.5, exact p without an epsilon (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: it fixes two statistical definitions in
> `emse_stats_extensions.py` that disagreed with the definition they claim.
> `cohens_g` returned **2g** (0–1), not Cohen's g (0–0.5);
> `binom_exact_two_sided` compared with a `1e-12` tolerance for `p=0.5`,
> lifting the 113/0 tail of **1.926e-34** to ~1.93e-12. Fix: g uses the
> effectsize definition `abs(n10−n01)/(2*(n10+n01))`; the exact tail uses
> integer `math.comb` weights, and the non-0.5 branch keeps probability
> ordering. The protected 20261016 archive is untouched and corrected values
> are reissued under 20261021. Manual:
> `docs/reviews/STATS_DEFINITION_AZ_2026-10-21.md`.

### Fixed — Cohen's g returns to the standard scale

- `cohens_g`: the denominator restores the factor 2, returning
  `abs(n10−n01)/(2*(n10+n01))` in 0–0.5 and satisfying the effectsize
  identity `max/(sum) − 0.5`.
- Real batches: R-P0-2 aitester vs df **0.370** (was 0.739), df vs plain
  LLM **0.500** (was 1.000), E6 **0.423** (was 0.846), E4 **0.500** (was 1.000).

### Fixed — the exact binomial tail is no longer lifted by an epsilon

- `binom_exact_two_sided`: the `p=0.5` branch compares integer weights and
  drops `+ 1e-12`; 113/0 goes from 1.93144963207924e-12 back to
  **1.925929944387236e-34**; 12/80 goes from 1.073374741074801e-12 back to
  **1.715599535972955e-13**.
- The non-0.5 branch keeps probability-ordering two-sided p, with a new
  independent cross lock (`k=0, n=10, p=0.1` → `1 − pmf(1) = 0.612579511`).

### Changed — artifact reissue and citation propagation

- Added `experiments/results/emse_stats_extensions_20261021/`
  (README + JSON + SHA256SUMS); the 20261016 archive is preserved
  byte-for-byte; `reproduce_zero_llm` verifies both generations.
- Paper `g = 0.739` → 0.370, EMSE skeleton range → 0.37–0.50, replication
  package path re-pointed to 20261021, and the X-round review gains an
  append-only errata (0.7391 was 2g, not Cliff's δ).
- Regression locks `tests/test_emse_stats_definition_az.py` **17 cases** +
  4 net new in the extensions test; **mutation M1 11 red / M2 4 red**
  (collected constant at 107, sha256 byte restore).

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AU round: on the experiment side, unknown is not zero — no number when unreadable, no partial sums posing as full sums, and AT write-rejection markers must not be lost (zero LLM, $0)

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AT round: token counting on the write side has a value domain too — a rejected write is not zero, and every rejection must be traceable (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: after rounds AI–AS separated "zero / absent /
> unreadable" on the read side layer by layer, the write side still turned bad
> values into counts silently with `int(... or 0)`: bool became 1, floats were
> truncated, numeric strings were accepted, negatives entered the totals, and
> `nan`/`inf` or unparsable strings crashed; a bad cache-file `tokens` value could
> even turn a genuine cache hit into a genuine LLM call. The fix routes
> `record_usage` / `record_cache_hit_usage` through the shared `count_reason`
> predicate, records no counts on rejection while still counting the event, and
> writes mechanism names to `token_write_reasons` / `cache_write_reasons`; readers
> treat write-rejection markers as unreadable, and `write_rejection_count`
> separates a cache `tokens: null` "unknown" from historical absence. Booklet:
> `docs/reviews/TOKEN_WRITE_DOMAIN_AT_2026-10-21.md`.

### Fixed — the write side no longer rewrites token counts silently

- `record_usage` / `record_cache_hit_usage`: both fields go through `count_reason`;
  any invalid value writes no counts at all (no partial sums) but still increments
  the `llm_calls` / `cache_hits` event and records the mechanism in
  `token_write_reasons` / `cache_write_reasons`.
- `_record_response_usage`: only `None` keeps the historical zero; numeric strings
  / bool / float / non-finite values are no longer swallowed or truncated by
  `int()`, but rejected with a disclosure; fail-closed when the budget is enabled.
- The cache-hit path keeps the raw `tokens`: a bad value or half schema records the
  hit as "hit with unknown tokens" and must not fall back to a real LLM call.

### Changed — a rejection becomes a readable state, not zero

- `TokenUsage.as_dict()` writes `token_write_reasons` / `cache_write_reasons` only
  when non-empty; `merge()` sums both mechanism counters (legacy records have no
  key, so the return domain is unchanged).
- Readers: `row_token_counts` / `row_token_reading` / `row_total_token_reading` /
  `cache_caliber` return unreadable (`None` + reasons) for
  `token_write_rejected:<mech>` / `cache_write_rejected:<mech>` — no zero, no
  partial sums.
- `otel_export._token_attributes` exports no token attributes on write-rejection
  markers (reusing AQ's disclosure channel).
- `write_rejection_count()` lets callers separate "there was genuinely no cache
  usage" (historical 0) from "cache usage is unknown" (a write rejection during
  this call) by difference.

- `tests/test_token_write_domain_at.py` **62 cases**: real writes 15 / cache writes
  11 / rejection counting 2 / response normalisation 12 / read-side markers 11 /

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AR round: the OTel exporter's identifiers must be legal before they can be stable — one trace, 32/16 hex, deterministic derivation (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: after AQ closed the numeric value domain, the same
> identifier fact still had three fates at the export boundary — leaked verbatim
> (a 16-hex `run_id` used as trace_id, a 12-hex `span_id`, uppercase, non-hex,
> all-zero), random fallback (a fresh uuid for missing identifiers on every
> export), or cross-trace breakage (a node's `run_id` overwrote the file-level
> trace, so its parent pointed at another trace's root). The fix adds five private
> predicates / derivators, canonicalises identifiers to 32/16 lowercase hex, keeps
> one trace per file, derives missing/invalid identifiers deterministically from
> SHA-256, re-derives collisions with a disclosure, and exports only `str` string
> attributes. Booklet:
> `docs/reviews/OTEL_EXPORT_IDENTIFIER_DOMAIN_AR_2026-10-21.md`.

### Fixed — legal identifiers, one trace, closed parents, stable repeat exports

- `_canonical_identifier`: identifiers accept only a non-empty `str` of hex digits,
  no wider than the field, not all-zero; lowercase + left zero-pad to 32/16 chars;
  non-str / empty / non-hex / too-long / all-zero values are not exported raw and
  are named per field (`run_id_not_string:<T>` / `run_id_invalid_format` /
  `span_id_not_string:<T>` / `span_id_invalid_format`).
- `_file_trace_id`: one trace_id per file — first canonicalisable `run_id` → SHA-256
  of the first non-empty invalid string → SHA-256 of `path:<path>`; a record-level
  `run_id` no longer overwrites the file trace, and a mismatch discloses
  `run_id_mismatch`.
- `_derived_span_id` / `_ensure_unique_span`: missing / invalid identifiers are
  derived as `SHA-256("aitester-span:{trace}:{index}:{attempt}")`; a duplicate
  `span_id` within a trace keeps the first occurrence, re-derives the later one and
  appends `span_id_duplicate`; the synthetic root no longer uses uuid.
- `_span_name`: non-node ⇒ `task_<event>`; a node name accepts only a non-empty
  `str`, while non-str / empty values fall back to `"node"` and disclose
  `node_not_string:<T>` / `node_empty`.
- String attributes: `decision` / `decision_reason` / `strategy_selected` /
  `stop_reason` / `task` export only `str`; non-str values are named per field and
  not exported raw.

### Changed — clean records keep their attributes verbatim; identifiers are canonicalised

- Full real corpus: 9086 files / 129058 spans; **exactly one** trace_id per file,
  all trace/span ids 32/16 lowercase hex, every parent inside the same file's span
  set, no duplicate span ids within a file, `export_value_reasons` **0 instances**;
  exporting the same file twice returns **byte-identical** results (9086/9086).
- Pre-fix measurement: 8002 files with >1 trace_id, 61188 broken parent links,
  9086/9086 files with unstable identifiers across two exports. **This round
  deliberately changes clean-export identifiers** — the regression criterion is
  "the same file exports identically twice", not "identical to pre-AR"; attributes
  (numeric and string) are unchanged (AQ numeric semantics hold).
- No archived or raw batch JSON was rewritten.

### Tests — 48 cases + 16/16 mutation anchors

- `tests/test_otel_export_identifier_domain_ar.py` **48 cases**: canonicalisation 10 +
  record mapping 11 + file trace 4 + duplicates 4 + string domain 11 + reason order 1 +
  end-to-end 5 + real corpus 2; `tests/test_p2_1_otel_export.py` rewrites its
  identifier assertions to the new caliber (case count unchanged at 7), and
  `tests/test_otel_export_value_domain_aq.py` swaps fixtures to valid hex (case
  count unchanged at 61).
- Mutations: 16/16 anchors red, 0 survivors, collected constant at 147,

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AQ round: the OTel exporter exports only verifiable numbers — bad tokens do not leak, bad timestamps do not abort a whole file (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: the export boundary wrote record numbers into span
> attributes verbatim. The same bad value had three fates here — leaked verbatim
> (NaN/Inf/string/bool), silently dropped (non-object `token_usage`, present

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-21 AN round: three token aggregation readers held their own `or 0` too — unreadable is not zero, and a partial sum is not a total (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: after AM collapsed the row-level policy into the
> shared reader, the three **aggregation** consumers still summed
> `(r.get("token_usage") or {}).get(..., 0)` each on its own. The same bad row
> crashed the write path, silently became 0 in the offline report, and produced a
> partial sum in the old-JSON fallback. The fix moves aggregation into
> `aggregate_row_token_usage` and separates "the whole batch has no such key"
> (historical 0) from "half schema / bad value" (`None`). Booklet:
> `docs/reviews/TOKEN_USAGE_AGGREGATE_AN_2026-10-21.md`.

### Fixed — the aggregation layer no longer folds unreadable tokens into 0 or a partial sum

- `row_token_reading` migrated from AM into `src/budget/token_usage.py`; new
  `aggregate_row_token_usage`: a whole-key absence / `null` ⇒ historical 0 and
  counted in `n_absent_rows`; a field that is present but bool / float / str /
  nan / inf / negative, or a positive triple with a missing field ⇒
  `input/output/total` all `None`, with `n_unreadable_rows` + `reading_reasons`;
  a non-object `token_usage` makes the triple, the call count and the cache all
  unreadable at once.
- `llm_calls` is judged independently: a bad call count voids only the call count,
  not the tokens; `in+out != total` keeps the total readable and only writes
  `n_token_split_mismatch_rows` (there is no money at the aggregation layer).
- Cache goes through `cache_totals`: a whole-batch old schema ⇒ `present=False`
  (consumer-side historical 0); half schema / bad values / non-object ⇒
  `hits` / `avoided` both `None` plus the mechanism name.
- Three consumers wired: `run_benchmark._aggregate_token_metrics`,
  `trusted_verification.arm_trusted_metrics`,
  `rag_analysis._token_metrics_from_details`; the old CLI's literal
  "命中 X / 调用 X + 真实" denominator now prints the real `llm_calls`.
- `statistical_analysis._row_cost_tokens` became a `row_token_reading` alias
  (AM / AL locks untouched).

### Changed — real-batch readings and old-schema consumers key-for-key unchanged

- All 783 main-batch rows across 9 arms are int and self-consistent with the
  cache schema absent ⇒ the five-key `token_metrics` recompute is bit-identical
  arm by arm; the repo-wide census counts 11197 rows / 337 arms, of which 1218
  are absent (historical 0) and 0 bad / 0 partial / 0 contradictions; protected

- Disclosure keys are written only when they actually happen:
  `n_token_unreadable_rows` / `token_reading_reasons` /
  `n_token_split_mismatch_rows` / `cache_reading_reasons`.

> This round adds no capability: it disposes AH section 7 items 1–3 (the `tokens_per_task`

### Fixed — a row's token accounting is three non-negative integers

- `token_usage` absent / `null` / non-object / empty object, a missing field, `bool` /
  float / string / negative / non-finite: these used to fold to 0, crash, count `True`
  as 1, carry `-5` into a negative amount, or turn shares into `nan` via `inf`
  (`inf != inf` being false let AH's closure check pass); each now names its mechanism
  and the whole arm's `tokens/task` and `$/task` are `None` — no zero folding, no partial sums.

  `input+output != total_tokens`: the token total stays readable and only the amount is
  voided (`token_split_mismatch:<in+out>/<total>` and friends), and per the AG discipline a
  `by_model` that is present but unreadable no longer also reports `no_model_attribution` —
  following the wrong hint will not turn anything green.

  bootstrap CI becomes `None`.

- `_cost_per_task` and `_bootstrap_cost_ci` now share `_read_tokens` (each used to write
  its own `or 0`); four helpers added: `token_count_reason` / `_row_token_counts` /
  `_reason_summary` / `_read_tokens`.
- `tokens_per_task` becomes `float | None`, the CI `tuple[float, float] | None`; the
  renderer prints `—（无 token 读数）` / `—`, and `build_report`'s bootstrap key may be `null`.
- A genuine zero must be written as three explicit 0s: `token_usage: {}` moves from 0.0 to
  "whole arm has no reading" (a behaviour change relative to AH, see booklet section 7 item 2).

> artifacts repo-wide, no gate) and 5.7 (`run_b8._write_json`'s `allow_nan=True`), and
> corrects a measurement misreading in 5.6 with a dated erratum. Booklet:
> `docs/reviews/JSON_STRICT_AF_2026-10-20.md`.

### Added — strict serialization primitive `src/utils/json_strict.py`

- `nonfinite_pointers(obj)` locates NaN/±Infinity recursively (including dict keys) and
  returns JSON paths (`$.arms[1].cost`, `$.x[<key nan>]`); shared and self-referential
  containers are neither duplicated nor followed forever.
- `strict_json_dumps(...)`: any non-finite value raises `NonFiniteJSONError` (with paths
  and the total count, "and N more" beyond five); otherwise
  `json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False)` as a second line of defence.
- **No silent null coercion**: a non-finite value usually signals an upstream defect, and
  writing it as `null` would just be another kind of silence.

### Fixed — four central write paths now serialize strictly

- `src/utils/atomic_io.atomic_write_json`: the failure happens before the temp file is
  created, so the old target is never touched.
- `experiments/run_b8_injection._write_json`: aggregate reports can no longer emit bare
  `NaN`/`Infinity`.
- `experiments/run_b8_injection._Injection._record`: a record holding a non-finite value
  now fails explicitly instead of writing a bad half line.
- `src/observability/trace.py`, three serialization sites: "better to miss a record than
  to write a bad one" is preserved -- a bad record is dropped whole with a warning while
  **the file itself remains strictly parseable line by line**.

### Fixed — `allow_nan=False` added to 41 direct write sites

39 source files, 41 write sites (by file: `src/` 8, `experiments/` 17, `scripts/` 14;
by site: 8 / 19 / 14). The gate re-scans all 41; violations: 0.

### Added — repo-wide gate `scripts/gates/check_json_strict.py` (`make gates` + CI)

- Artifact side: every `.json` / `.jsonl` from `git ls-files` is parsed strictly
  (`.jsonl` line by line with line numbers), falling back to `rglob` outside git;
  measured **7273 artifacts = 7271 strict + 2 registered exemptions + 0 violations**.
- Source side: an AST scan of `src|experiments|scripts` -- `json.dump`, and any
  `json.dumps` inside the argument chain of
  `write`/`writelines`/`write_text`/`atomic_write_text`/`stdout.write`, must carry a
  literal `allow_nan=False`; **300 source files, 0 sink violations**.
- No vacuous green: an empty scan set fails outright; the 2 A20 historical truncated
  traces are exempted per path, and **an exempt file that becomes strictly parseable is
  reported as exemption drift**.

### Changed — AE section 5.6 measurement erratum (append only, AE text untouched)

AE's "68 files" was a text-grep count, not a count of bare-token violations: strict
parsing of every controlled artifact found **0 violations**; the 69 files under
`experiments/results/` (42 tracked) contain `NaN`/`Infinity` only inside string values
(test names such as `test_sqrt_positive_infinity`, diagnostic text "x is NaN"), which is
legal JSON. The lesson is mechanized as two locks: the gate never counts string-embedded
text as a violation, and the serializer neither escapes nor deletes it.

### Tests — 28 cases + 9/9 mutation anchors

- `tests/test_json_strict_af.py`, **28 cases**: serializer path naming 8, atomic
  write / run_b8 fail-closed 4, trace drop-not-corrupt 3, gate 7 (including a real-repo
  run and "NaN inside a string is not a violation"), library-level 6.
- Mutation anchors M1–M9 each turned red (8 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1), zero
  0-red anchors; baseline 28 passed, collected constant at 28, `compile()` before every
  write, sha256 assertion after restore. M3/M4/M5 additionally trip the real-repo gate
  case, showing the gate is an independent second lock against sink regressions.

### Close-out

- Full suite: **10351 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed** (collected 10356, +28), 191.66s;
  coverage lines **18486/19009 = 97.2487%**, branches **6674/7110 = 93.8678%**
  (every new line covered).
- Pre-registration run 10349 passed / 2 failed / 5 skipped: ① the baseline guard
  (BASELINE not yet refreshed); ② **a real defect introduced this round** -- a CI step
  `name` containing an unquoted `AF: ` caused a YAML ScannerError, caught by

- A **third** self-catch came from the `make gates` chain (the pre-existing AO3 header

  AF -- the phrase was advanced per that lock's own maintenance convention (not a lock

- Close-out re-run: after those fixes `make gates` was re-run **alone**, rc=0,
  10351 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed in **183.51s** (the in-chain suite runs without

- No committed artifact rewritten; the 2 A20 historical truncated traces kept byte-exact

- Boundaries: the gate only recognises a literal `allow_nan=False` (runtime-assembled

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-20 AD round: statistical-quantity rendering preserves magnitude + the normal-tail complement pattern eliminated + a repo-wide census of silent precision-loss patterns (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: a repo-wide census along the AC-1 defect class, disposing the two items registered in round AC, with every remaining same-family site judged individually.

### Fixed — `_fmt_stat_num` printed every nonzero small magnitude as "0.0000" (AD-1, display precision)

- `{:.4f}` silently printed every nonzero |v| < 5e-5 as "0.0000" — the magnitude information was destroyed. This was exactly the AC-1 visibility gap: p=5.890715e-26 (the exact value at χ²=111.01) and the pre-fix underflowed p=0.0 looked identical in reports (both displayed "0.0000 (***)"), so a reader could not tell "an exactly computed tiny value" from "lost precision" on the face of the ledger.
- Fix: nonzero and |v| < 1e-4 → `{:.2e}` scientific notation (5.890715e-26 → "5.89e-26", 1.811017e-07 → "1.81e-07"); exact 0.0 still renders "0.0000" (zero is a legitimate statistic, e.g. χ²=0 / no discordant pairs); -0.0 keeps its sign (pre-existing `{:.4f}` behavior); nan/inf and normal-magnitude rendering unchanged. The main batch's plain-df report cell is locked end to end as "5.89e-26".
- Historical artifacts are not rewritten: existing reports such as the canonical `statistical_report.md` keep their original rendering (dated-errata discipline); the improvement applies to future regenerations.

### Fixed — the normal-tail complement pattern in `emse_testlevel_detection` (AD-2)

- `1.0 - _normal_cdf(z)` is the same shape as AC-1's `1 - chi2.cdf`: for z ≳ 8.2, `1.0 - cdf` silently becomes 0.0 through floating-point precision. Switched to the erfc survival function `0.5·erfc(z/√2)` (exact for z < ~27). The field is round-displayed, so readings in the displayable range are digit-identical — what changed is the pattern itself.

### Verified — repo-wide census of silent precision-loss patterns (four classes, each site judged)

| Pattern | Sites | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Complement `1 − cdf` | `statistical_analysis.mcnemar_test` (fixed in AC-1), `emse_testlevel_detection` (fixed in AD-2) | Both disposed |
| Complement `1 − prod` | `statistical_analysis._pass_at_k_value` | Benign: on underflow the true value is 1.0 to machine precision, and k>n−c already has a constant-1.0 branch |
| Product `p·(1−p)` | Wilson CI (`emse_stats_report` / `pass_matched_sensitivity`) | Benign: a product, not a complement; at p=1 the factor is exactly 0 |
| Division `(po−pe)/(1−pe)` | Cohen's κ (`e7_adjudication`) | Benign: pe≥1 already guarded, returning None |
| `exp(log diff)` | BF10 (`emse_quixbugs_specir_expand` / `emse_optimization`) | Benign: underflow to 0.0 is the intended "evidence for H0" semantics |
| `inv_cdf(1−α/2)` | `emse_stats_report` z critical value | Benign: α is the constant 0.05, never near 1 |
| Float equality `== 1.0` | Protocol 0/1 value consumers (`four_channel_recompute` / `pass_matched_sensitivity` / `emse_quixbugs_specir_expand`) | Consistent idiom: the producer `_compute_detection_rate` only writes literals 1.0/0.0/None; no equality on computed values |
| Catastrophic cancellation | `rag_ab_experiment._var` / `stvr_statistical_analysis` (stdlib) | Benign: two-pass `sum((x−m)²)` is numerically stable |

Regression locks: `tests/test_ad_round_stat_display.py`, **11 cases** (7 AD-1 rendering + 3 AD-2 tail + 1 end to end); mutation-verified: reverting each fix turns 7 targeted cases red, all green after restore.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-20 AC round: fix for the McNemar p `1−cdf` floating-point underflow + E7 toolchain dry run + AB-17 wiring audit (zero LLM, $0)

> This round adds no capability: an independent recompute audit found one numerical defect in the statistics layer and fixed it, plus a dry run of the E7 adjudication toolchain and a wiring audit of the AB-17 close-out (both pass, no new defects).

### Fixed — `mcnemar_test`'s p value underflows to exactly 0.0 in the chi-square tail (AC-1)

- `experiments/statistical_analysis.mcnemar_test` computed p as `1.0 - chi2.cdf(x, df=1)`. With float64 machine epsilon ~2.2e-16 relative to 1, `1.0 - cdf` equals 1.0 whenever p ≲ 6e-17 (χ² ≳ 71), so p **silently became exactly 0.0**. The main batch's plain_llm_df vs plain_llm (χ²=111.00885) was measured on the old path as p=0.0 / BH q=0.0, while the exact values are p=5.890715e-26 / q=1.767215e-25 (`erfc(√(χ²/2))` and `chi2.sf` agree digit for digit).
- **Impact**: the "raw p / standard BH q" quoted in the Z-round closure report and the `statistical_report_3seed_pooled.md` erratum section were previously **irreproducible from the production code path** — the Z-round regression locks (`test_review_20261019_stats.py`) used a test-local erfc helper, and the production `mcnemar_test` was never executed on the main-batch data (the same "logic tested, wiring untested" blind spot). The significance conclusions (all three ***) are unaffected.
- Fix: `p = chi2.sf(x, df=1)` (survival function, numerically stable in the tail); the two detection comparisons with χ²≤48.79 and all repair comparisons are unaffected (1−cdf and sf agree within 1e-12 relative for p≥1e-14); the canonical `statistical_report.md` passed table's χ²=123.1419 row has the same underflow (p 0.0000 → exact ≈1.4e-28), but its rendering and conclusions are unchanged because the display format is `{:.4f}`.
- Regression locks: `tests/test_ac_round_mcnemar_tail.py`, **6 cases** (production-path main-batch p/q truth closing the recompute chain + χ² cross-checked against the pooled report + two synthetic huge-χ² no-underflow cases + moderate-χ² values unchanged + existing boundary semantics preserved); mutation-verified: reverting to `1−cdf` turns three cases red, all green after restore.
- Methodology lesson (a trap in the test itself): `pytest.approx`'s default `abs=1e-12` lets an underflowed 0.0 **pass** as a 1e-25-magnitude truth — AC-round assertions use `abs=0.0` (purely relative) throughout.
- Artifacts: `statistical_report_3seed_pooled.md` gains a dated 2026-10-20 erratum section (defect / fix / impact surface), `main_batch/SHA256SUMS` refreshed accordingly (only that file's line changed; all 2040 entries verify).

### Verified — E7 adjudication toolchain dry run and AB-17 seven-read-site wiring audit (zero LLM)

- E7 toolchain: `validate` passes on all three blank entry sheets (n=8/41/72); out-of-scale judgments fail closed; unfilled rows are refused at `merge`; a synthetically filled pair exercises Cohen's κ + 10,000 bootstraps + the confusion matrix + the disagreement-row listing (dry-run data in `/tmp`, artifacts untouched).
- AB-17: all seven price-table read sites are wired through the shared `src/budget/pricing.py` helpers (`pricing` itself + `spec_examples_generator` / `emse_stats_report` / `emse_stats_extensions` / `statistical_analysis` / `analyze_t1_b2_main_batch` / `run_b8_injection`), with no "declared but unconsumed" gap.
- Baseline: collected **10294** = passed **10289** + skipped 5 + failed 0 (net +6 cases; sandbox-host measurement on this machine: 10275 passed / 19 skipped / 0 failed); `experiments/` is outside the `--cov=src` scope, and `coverage.xml` measures 18440/18963 lines = 97.24% and 6652/7090 arcs = 93.82% (each 1 off the AB-17 registration, inside the registered race-branch ±2 jitter band); ruff / mypy / all gates green.

## [Unreleased] — 2026-10-20 Round AB: real-corpus replay falsifies a synthetic-enumeration premise, a documented criterion becomes an executable artifact, dataset-adapter tolerance backfill, silently-dropped table cells fixed under a repo-wide criterion, the `json.loads` return domain closed at six sites, the `experiments/` return domain censused with one silent denominator turned into disclosed counts, absence and unreadability separated from zero hits, the three shapes of absence split into three buckets at three analysis sites, evidence-based coverage close-out, five registered sites closed in one go (a race branch locked instead of pragma-ed, three absence mechanisms named, non-object trace rows out of the denominator, loader row-set collapse made visible, the price-table `None` sentinel split three ways, the currency gate that `total_usd` never asserted, and the currency judgement collapsed into one predicate wired into all five sites, a rejected amount never wearing the shape of an amount with its attribution from the same decision, and the price-admission domain written once, and the table-level read-side admission written once) (zero LLM, $0)

> Every claim in this round replaces one kind of weak evidence with a stronger one:
> ① a **universal proposition** ("permanently unreachable") replaced by
> **observation + mechanism** (zero triggers on the real corpus, plus a structural
> argument for why such fragments can never be rescued); ② a criterion published as
> **prose in a document** replaced by a script the test suite **executes at runtime**
> (document and lock become the same artifact — whichever drifts turns red);
> ③ "coverage is not green" no longer treated as a defect by default: reachable sites
> get mutation-verified locks driven by genuine malformed input, and what cannot be
> reached is registered with its mechanism — no fabricated mocks, no
> `# pragma: no cover`. Scope discipline: raw experiment data (batch JSON) was
> **not rewritten**. Real LLM spend: **$0**.

### Changed — redundancy verdict for the tier-2 (first-object repair) tier in `helpers.py` (AB-1 / AB-2)

- **Real-corpus replay**: `experiments/helpers_tier_replay.py` feeds the product's own
  LLM response cache into `extract_json_object` and counts four layers separately —
  **692** reached tier 2, **667** produced a fragment, **1** scanner-divergent, and the
  tier-2 return branch **would actually fire 0** times (7,565 responses, no corrupt
  files). Two independent implementations agree line by line; the same input yields a
  byte-identical output.
- **AA-5's premise is falsified**: "tier 1 and this tier take the same fragment from the
  same first `{`, so tier 1 already tried everything" does not hold for that 1 divergent
  sample — tier 1 returns **`None`** for it (the whole repair block is skipped), making
  tier 2 the **first and only** tier that produces a candidate and repairs it for that
  input class. The `helpers.py` comment now drops both the universal wording and the
  false premise.
- **Replaced by a mechanism argument**: divergence requires a **bare backslash outside
  strings** inside the tier-2 fragment, and none of the five candidates removes
  backslashes ⇒ such fragments are unrescuable. Targeted enumeration of the divergent
  class: **716 inputs, 0 rescuable**, pinned as `TestDivergentClassUnrescuable` (a future
  "remove `\`" candidate turns that lock red first, instead of discovering a semantic
  drift after deletion).
- **Disposition: tier 2 is kept** — same decision, new basis. `TestDeletionEquivalenceProbe`
  verifies byte-identical output with and without tier 2 across four pinned input classes,
  so deleting it currently only saves five doomed parse attempts; but "no change to the
  return value" remains the agreement of three empirical lines, not a proof, and deletion
  is a behaviour change that needs its own round with the equivalence lock in hand.
- **Privacy discipline**: the script emits **aggregate counts plus a sha256 digest of the
  file-name list** and never a response body; if the cache directory is absent it
  **fail-closes with exit code 2** (no "all-zero but looks executed" report). All regression
  locks run against a synthetic `tmp_path` fake cache and never touch the user's real cache.

### Added — spec_ir_v2 product self-check locks + a stale priority retracted (AB-3)

- 3 cases: an **adversarial `target_function`** (its name carries a newline and a quote, making
  the rendered product syntactically illegal) drives the "parse the product, discard the whole
  block on failure" branch of both the oracle and the SMT-witness chains to line level (confirmed
  by trace) — the only interception point that keeps bad code out of the execution chain, previously
  asserted in prose only.
- Registered that the "no-assert check" inside the `_compile_smt_witness_tests` loop (formerly line
  2014) is **fully shadowed by the entry guard and permanently unreachable**; pinned as a reverse
  lock instead of fabricating a mock to "cover" it.
- **Retracted** ROUND3 §4 ②, which listed `_precondition_witness_binding`'s conservative bounds as
  "to be covered": those four bounds already had 7 locks (landed in the same AA-5 batch).

### Added — the AA-8 criterion becomes an executable artifact (AB-4)

- 2 cases in `tests/test_llm_oms_leaf_fallback.py::TestProcessStateReaderEnumeration`:
  the test **executes the AST criterion script published in `docs/MEASUREMENT_INTEGRITY.md` §8**
  and reconciles its result against the `KNOWN_READERS` set registered in the lock — document and
  lock are now the same artifact, so a fifth reader turns both red together. The second case pins
  this file's own isolation discipline (removing the autouse reset fixture turns it red). That
